newsitem.title: UK: British pro-Europeans detect swing towards EMU.
newsitem.headline: British pro-Europeans detect swing towards EMU.

text.p: Pro-European politicians on Thursday welcomed an opinion poll which they said showed a major shift of opinion in Britain towards adopting a planned European Union single currency and indicated they could win a referendum on the issue.

The poll, conducted by Gallup for the European Movement pressure group, showed the proportion of Britons strongly opposed to giving up the pound has fallen to 22 percent from 36 percent in August last year.
There is still a small majority against Britain joining a single currency in 1999, when it is due to be launched, the poll indicated.
It said 41 percent of the 1,001 people questioned earlier this month tended to support early British membership while 52 percent were opposed.
But two-thirds of the polling sample said they were open to persuasion on the issue.
European Movement chairman Giles Radice said: "This poll blows the single currency debate wide open."

Radice, a Labour MP, added: "Many people will be surprised that three-quarters of the British people are either open to persuasion that Britain should join the single currency or are already in favour."
Quentin Davies, a Conservative MP who is one of the Movement's vice-chairmen, said: "I believe it is increasingly possible to see a national consensus on the decision that Britain ought to take."

European Commissioner Neil Kinnock, a former leader of the Labour Party, said the poll showed that the vast majority of Britons "now declare themselves openly in favour of closer cooperation with the other 14 countries of the EU."
Prime Minister Tony Blair has pledged to put any proposal by his government to take Britain into a single currency to a referendum.
